title: “Airport Free Wi-Fi” wants your email password
scenario: A Wi-Fi network named after the airport opens a polished captive portal with airport branding. It offers free access if you “verify your identity” by signing in with Google or Microsoft.

answers.A: Ask airport staff for the official network name and connect only through the expected captive portal without handing over an unrelated account password.
answers.B: Use mobile data to check the airport website for Wi-Fi instructions before connecting.
answers.C: Use the Google/Microsoft sign-in because single sign-on is safer than creating a new airport password.

explanation: A network name and logo are not authentication. Public Wi-Fi should not need credentials to an unrelated high-value account.
proTip: Free Wi-Fi should not cost your email identity.
